detailedExplanation: Verified against The Tiffin Girls’ School Year 9 Chemistry Curriculum Outline 2026–27 (AQA GCSE Chemistry 8462).
Cracking breaks large hydrocarbon molecules into smaller, more useful molecules. The feedstock is vaporised and heated strongly, often over a hot catalyst.
The products include shorter alkanes and alkenes. Alkenes are especially useful as chemical feedstocks because their carbon–carbon double bond makes them more reactive than alkanes.
For equation questions, check that the total number of carbon and hydrogen atoms is conserved.
